newsitem.title: USA: Jefferson-Pilot sees Chubb deal accretive.
newsitem.headline: Jefferson-Pilot sees Chubb deal accretive.

text.p: Jefferson-Pilot Corp said Tuesday it expects its acquisition of Chubb Corp's life insurance business to have a breakeven impact on earnings in the first year after the closing and to contribute to earnings thereafter.

Jefferson-Pilot, which announced Monday a definitive agreement to buy Chubb's life insurance operation for $875 million in cash, said it expects the Chubb business to be accretive to earnings by at least eight percent, or a contribution of $25-$30 million.

The company expects to cut costs at both Chubb Life and its other insurance operations, for total combined savings of about $40 million, Chief Executive David Stonecipher said in a meeting late Monday, company spokesman Michael Burney said.

Stonecipher said it was too early to say how many positions might be eliminated in the merger, but he said the company plans to keep a major base of operations in Concord, N.H., where Chubb Life is based.
Jefferson-Pilot also plans for the Chubb Life business to maintain a distribution relationship with Chubb Corp's property-casualty agents, Burney said.
"We expect the distribution relationship will continue with Chubb Corp, whose property-casualty agents have generated 20 percent of Chubb Life's total production," he said.
"He (Stonecipher) believes this relationship can be even more beneficial to both parties," Burney added.
The Chubb Life business will be renamed by Jefferson-Pilot, he said.

With the Chubb acquisition, which is expected to close as soon as regulatory approvals are obtained, Jefferson-Pilot will rank in the top 15 of U.S. life insurance companies in total life premium income.
Although Jefferson-Pilot may make additional acquisitions, Stonecipher expects the company to be preoccupied with integrating Chubb Life, its largest acquisition to date, Burney said.
"That's where our focus will be," Burney said.
However, he said, Jefferson-Pilot will still have a cushion of several hundred million dollars following the Chubb Life purchase.
This would give Jefferson-Pilot "some flexibility if something came along," Burney said.
Jefferson-Pilot is still publicly searching for a partner to help it launch an HMO business and considers its Jefferson-Pilot Communications Co a core business.
